name: Dersimelagon
summary: MT-7117, an investigational oral MC1R agonist that darkens skin pigment to protect people with light-sensitivity disorders; it is not a tanning product and has no looks-related trials.
lead: Dersimelagon (formerly MT-7117; developed as dersimelagon phosphoric acid) is an investigational, orally administered, nonpeptide small-molecule selective agonist of the melanocortin 1 receptor (MC1R) . Activation of MC1R drives melanogenesis in pigment cells and also has anti-inflammatory and antifibrotic effects .

name: Semax
summary: A Russian ACTH(4-10)-derived nootropic peptide with small stroke trials in Russia and a following in 'study-maxxing' circles; it has no studied effect on appearance.
lead: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) that combines an ACTH(4-7) fragment with a Pro-Gly-Pro tail, giving a long-lasting analogue of ACTH(4-10) without hormonal activity . It was developed in Russia and is described in Russian literature as a nootropic and neuroprotective agent .
claims: Semax improves focus and studying, including for ADHD
It does not do much ("cope")
Semax is safe for teenagers
Semax boosts libido as a side benefit

name: Hydroxypinacolone retinoate
summary: HPR, sold as Granactive Retinoid, is a retinoic acid ester marketed as a gentler cosmetic retinoid; published human data are small and mostly use combination products.
lead: Hydroxypinacolone retinoate (HPR) is a synthetic retinoid ester that appears in cosmetic skincare, either on its own or alongside retinol or retinyl propionate . A 2021 stability study treated it as a newer retinoid in commercial cosmetics alongside retinol, retinyl palmitate and beta-carotene . It is sold under the trade name Granactive Retinoid, a trademarked mixture of 10% HPR in dimethyl isosorbide developed by Grant Industries, according to Grokipedia, which dates the product's introduction to late 2014 and says it was licensed to brands including The Ordinary .

name: Retinaldehyde (Retinal)
summary: The vitamin A form one step before retinoic acid, sold in OTC serums as a middle-ground retinoid; skin-specific human evidence is sparse and mostly old or still registered.
lead: Retinaldehyde, usually shortened to retinal, is the aldehyde form of vitamin A (retinol) with the formula C20H28O . In biology it is best known as the chromophore of vertebrate vision, where its 11-cis isomer binds opsin proteins, and as an intermediate that can be converted onward to retinoic acid . In cosmetic skincare, it is sold as a retinoid said to sit between retinol and tretinoin in strength.
claims: Retinal can be alternated with a prescription retinoid while skin adjusts
Retinal sits between retinol and tretinoin in strength

name: Trifarotene (Aklief)
summary: Aklief is an Rx RAR-gamma-selective retinoid cream approved in 2019 for acne on the face and trunk; large vehicle-controlled trials back it, and no anti-aging approval exists.
lead: Trifarotene, sold as Aklief (a 0.005% cream), is a topical retinoid developed by Galderma that selectively activates retinoic acid receptor gamma (RAR-gamma) and is classed as a fourth-generation retinoid . The US FDA approved it in October 2019 for the topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 9 years of age and older .
claims: Aklief is a reasonable step before isotretinoin when tretinoin has not worked
Trifarotene works on face and body acne
Topical retinoids are not enough for long-term remission
Aklief carries no significant systemic absorption concerns

name: Retinyl palmitate
summary: A storage-form vitamin A ester found in moisturisers, sunscreens and supplements; the weakest-studied cosmetic retinoid, with a long-running safety debate over its use on sun-exposed skin.
lead: Retinyl palmitate is an ester formed between retinol (vitamin A) and palmitic acid (formula C36H60O2), used in cosmetics, fortified foods and dietary supplements as a stable source of vitamin A . In skincare it is grouped among the first-generation retinoids, which also include all-trans retinoic acid, retinol and retinaldehyde, although it is not itself the active form and must be converted in tissue .
claims: Retinyl palmitate in sunscreen is hazardous
Retinyl palmitate is a weaker, gentler form of retinoid that still improves skin
Too much vitamin A from supplements is toxic

name: Poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra)
summary: Sculptra, an injectable PLLA collagen stimulator for midface volume and cheek lines; randomized trials and systematic reviews show effects lasting up to about two years, with nodules a known risk.
lead: Sculptra is a brand of injectable poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA), a synthetic, biocompatible and biodegradable polymer, marketed by Galderma as a collagen-stimulating dermal treatment . It is used to restore volume in the cheeks and midface, to soften nasolabial folds and cheek wrinkles, and, in its original indication, to correct facial lipoatrophy in HIV .
claims: Sculptra can fill out a gaunt face after weight loss
PLLA gives gradual, long-lasting collagen-based results rather than instant filling
Biostimulators help facial volume loss associated with GLP-1 weight loss

name: Deoxycholic acid (Kybella)
summary: Injectable fat-cell destroyer approved for double chins; works on a small area, with swelling and rare nerve injury.
lead: Deoxycholic acid is a secondary bile acid, produced when gut bacteria modify cholic acid, that normally helps emulsify dietary fats . A synthetic, injectable form is sold in the United States as Kybella and elsewhere as Belkyra. It is a prescription cytolytic drug that is injected under the skin to destroy fat cells, and it is approved for improving the appearance of moderate to severe convexity or fullness caused by submental fat (a "double chin") in adults .
claims: Kybella is a good non-surgical alternative to lipo for a small submental fat pad
It can be used in other areas such as the nasolabial fat pad

name: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) filler
summary: Permanent filler beads that stay in the face for good; few sources on outcomes, and removal is difficult if problems arise.
lead: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) filler is a non-absorbable injectable made of tiny PMMA microspheres suspended in a carrier gel, sold in the United States under names such as Artefill and Bellafill. Because the microspheres are not broken down by the body, the fillers are described as permanent: the particles stay in place and prompt the body to form fibrous tissue around them .
claims: PMMA is dangerous to put in the body
Bodybuilders use PMMA injections to enlarge muscles

name: Poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA)
summary: Collagen-stimulating injectable polymer related to PLLA; a handful of trials, nodules are the main known risk.
lead: Poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA) is a biodegradable synthetic polymer used in injectable skin products classed as biostimulators. Rather than simply filling a space, biostimulatory fillers such as PDLLA, poly-L-lactic acid (PLLA), polycaprolactone and calcium hydroxylapatite are described as prompting a controlled inflammatory response that leads the body to produce new collagen .

name: Collagen filler
summary: The original injectable filler; temporary and allergy-prone in bovine form, now largely overtaken by hyaluronic acid.
lead: Collagen fillers are injectable implants made from animal-derived or human bioengineered collagen, used to soften wrinkles and fold lines and to add soft-tissue volume. They are generally regarded as the original modern injectable dermal filler: a 2006 review notes that bovine collagen was the most popular injectable implant in the United States for nearly two decades before human bioengineered collagen products and hyaluronic acid fillers became available .

name: Polyacrylamide gel
summary: A permanent synthetic gel filler with little published cosmetic evidence in these sources; removal can be difficult.
lead: Polyacrylamide gel, in its injectable medical form polyacrylamide hydrogel (PAAG), is a water-based synthetic gel made of cross-linked polyacrylamide. It has been used as a permanent soft-tissue filler, including for facial contouring and for HIV-related facial fat loss, and the same type of material is used in other medical settings such as injections for urinary incontinence and, in a Danish trial, intra-articular injection for knee osteoarthritis .

name: Mercury skin lightening
summary: Toxic mercury-salt lightening creams banned in many countries but still found in informal markets; no clinical use.
lead: Mercury skin lightening refers to the use of creams, soaps and lotions containing mercury compounds to make the skin paler or to fade dark spots. The World Health Organization describes skin lightening as a dangerous practice often associated with exposure to mercury salts, which inhibit melanin production, and says mercury-containing lightening products are hazardous and have been banned in many countries .

name: Clobetasol propionate
summary: A super-potent prescription steroid that turns up in illicit lightening creams; its documented skin harms are significant.
lead: Clobetasol propionate is a super-high-potency topical corticosteroid, the top group in the seven-class US potency ranking . It is prescribed for corticosteroid-responsive skin conditions such as psoriasis, eczema, contact dermatitis, lichen sclerosus and lichen planus, and as a treatment for cutaneous graft-versus-host disease .

name: Decapeptide-12
summary: A cosmetic brightening peptide with only small, uncontrolled, multi-product studies behind it.
lead: Decapeptide-12 is a ten-amino-acid cosmetic peptide marketed for skin brightening. It is described in the literature as a novel peptide used to lighten hyperpigmentation, and a 2021 pharmaceutics paper characterises it as safer than hydroquinone in reducing melanin content, with efficacy of more than 50% over 16 weeks of twice-daily treatment, but limited by poor skin penetration because it is hydrophilic and large .

name: Rice water
summary: Starchy rice-rinse water used as a hair and skin wash in Asian folk beauty; popular, but no trials test it for hair or skin.
lead: Rice water is the cloudy, starchy liquid left after rice is rinsed, soaked or boiled. It carries starch along with small amounts of vitamins, minerals and amino acids leached from the grain, and it can also be left to ferment for a day or two before use. It has a long history of folk use in parts of Asia as a hair rinse and skin wash, and it is also used as an oral fluid for diarrhoea.

name: Turmeric (topical)
summary: Traditional yellow spice paste used for brightening; one small vitiligo trial exists, none for cosmetic lightening, and it stains.
lead: Topical turmeric refers to the use of turmeric root (Curcuma longa) or its main pigment curcumin on the skin, as a paste, mask or cream. It is a long-standing household and traditional preparation in South Asia, promoted in appearance communities as a brightening, evening and anti-blemish ingredient.

name: Powdered pearl
summary: Ground pearl used in Chinese medicine for a luminous complexion; research covers wound and bone repair, not skin brightening.
lead: Powdered pearl, or pearl powder, is finely ground pearl or nacre (mother-of-pearl), composed mainly of calcium carbonate with an organic protein matrix. It is a traditional Chinese medicine ingredient used for roughly two thousand years, and it is applied to the skin or taken by mouth for complexion and general health.

name: Trenbolone
summary: A potent veterinary-origin steroid used for a dry, hard physique; no human trials, and reviews report adverse effects in most users.
lead: Trenbolone, often called tren, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group. It is used in veterinary medicine as a growth promoter in cattle, usually as the acetate ester in implants, and it has never been approved for human medical use. It is used non-medically by bodybuilders and other athletes who want more muscle mass, strength and a lean, vascular look.
claims: Low-dose tren helps bone growth and final height.
Tren gives a dry, hard physique without water retention.
Tren is safe enough at low doses or for teenagers.
Tren changes mood and sexual behaviour.

name: Nandrolone
summary: A prescription-origin injectable steroid used for muscle; trials show lean-mass effects in sick patients, but none in healthy lifters.
lead: Nandrolone, also called 19-nortestosterone, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from testosterone by removal of one methyl group, and it is the parent compound of the 19-nor AAS subclass. It is usually given as an injectable ester, most often nandrolone decanoate (brand name Deca-Durabolin).
claims: Deca is 'hair safe' because it converts to a weak androgen.
Deca builds a lot of muscle, as shown by trials.
Deca improves bone growth.
Deca is not worth using alongside testosterone and HGH.

name: Oxandrolone
summary: An oral steroid with real clinical trial data in burns and wasting, popular as a mild cutting drug; its height claims conflict with growth studies.
lead: Oxandrolone, widely known by the brand name Anavar, is an oral synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from dihydrotestosterone. It carries a 17-alpha-methyl group and a distinctive oxygen atom in its ring, which are associated with strong anabolic effect and comparatively mild androgenic effect.
claims: Anavar can add height or complement growth hormone in teens.
Anavar is great for cutting.
Anavar is a mild addition to a first test cycle.

name: Stanozolol
summary: A famous oral/injectable doping steroid for a dry, lean look; it has an approved angioedema use but little appearance data and notable HDL and liver effects.
lead: Stanozolol, known by the brand name Winstrol, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) derived from dihydrotestosterone. It was developed in the early 1960s, is approved in the United States for prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema, and is also used in veterinary medicine. It is available as an oral tablet and as an injectable preparation.
claims: Winstrol and similar compounds help height growth.
Non-aromatising steroids are safe for growth plates.
Winstrol masculinises the face and physique.

name: Boldenone
summary: A horse steroid used by bodybuilders for slow, steady gains; no human trials exist.
lead: Boldenone is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS), the 1-dehydro analogue of testosterone. It is used mainly in veterinary medicine, usually as the long-acting undecylenate ester sold as Equipoise, for debilitated horses, and it is not approved for human therapeutic use in the United States.

name: Methandienone
summary: The classic oral bulking steroid (Dianabol): small controlled trials show lean-mass gain, with liver, blood-pressure and hormonal costs.
lead: Methandienone (also spelled metandienone or methandrostenolone, and sold as Dianabol or D-bol) is a synthetic oral anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from testosterone. It was one of the first anabolic steroids widely used by athletes and remains among the best-known in bodybuilding culture, where it is regarded as a traditional oral compound for gaining mass .
claims: Dianabol is the classic fast mass builder.
Gains from methandienone are largely water.
Published human research on the compound is scarce, so anecdote dominates.
Oral steroids can be run alongside injectables with support drugs to limit side effects.

name: Oxymetholone
summary: Anadrol: an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a potent oral bulker, with a well-documented liver-toxicity profile and almost no physique trials.
lead: Oxymetholone (brand names include Anadrol and Anapolon) is a synthetic oral anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It is a 17-alpha-alkylated compound, a structural change that allows oral dosing and that is associated with hepatic toxicity. Its medical role has been in anemias due to deficient red-cell production, such as aplastic anemia and Fanconi anemia.
claims: Anadrol is a powerful oral for fast mass and fullness.
Anadrol can masculinise the face and body.
Its reputation for harshness is overstated at low doses.
Orals like oxymetholone damage cholesterol far more than injectables.

name: Drostanolone
summary: Masteron: a DHT-derived injectable once used against breast cancer and now used by bodybuilders for a dry, hard look, with no appearance trials.
lead: Drostanolone (also dromostanolone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid that is a 2-alpha-methyl derivative of dihydrotestosterone. It is most often seen as drostanolone propionate, sold historically as Masteril and in bodybuilding circles as Masteron.
claims: Masteron gives a dry, hard, lean look.
Masteron can replace an aromatase inhibitor for controlling estrogen.
It may cause hair loss that finasteride cannot block.
Collagen and skin products can offset the skin effects of a large steroid stack.

name: Mesterolone
summary: Proviron: a mild oral DHT derivative used in medicine for male hypogonadism and fertility, and by forum users as an add-on for hardness and libido; appearance effects are untested.
lead: Mesterolone (brand name Proviron) is a synthetic oral androgen derived from dihydrotestosterone with a methyl group at the 1-alpha position. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes it as strongly androgenic and weakly anabolic, not aromatizable to estrogen, and associated with a low risk of liver toxicity.
claims: Proviron raises DHT and aids puberty-maxxing.
Proviron alone does little for muscle, hair or hardness.
It improves sperm count and fertility.
Raising DHT with Proviron will undo finasteride or increase hair loss.

name: Methyltestosterone
summary: An old oral testosterone analogue still used medically for hypogonadism and menopause; appearance and bodybuilding use is undocumented in trials and absent from the forum sources.
lead: Methyltestosterone is a synthetic androgen, a 17-alpha-methyl derivative of testosterone that can be taken by mouth. It has been used to treat male hypogonadism, and in women as part of menopausal hormone therapy, usually combined with esterified estrogens.

name: Fluoxymesterone
summary: Halotestin: a strong oral androgen from the 1950s that bodybuilders add for hardness and aggression; documented trials are in breast cancer and hypogonadism, none in appearance.
lead: Fluoxymesterone (brand name Halotestin; also Androxy) is a synthetic oral androgen and anabolic steroid derived from testosterone. A 1957 JAMA article already carried its name, and later literature describes its use as a replacement androgen in hypogonadism and, in women, as hormone therapy for advanced breast cancer.
claims: Halotestin adds hardness and strength more than size.
It makes users aggressive.
Oral fluoxymesterone is hard on the liver.
Some anabolic steroids, fluoxymesterone included, can promote height gain in short children.

name: Methenolone
summary: Primobolan: a mild DHT-derived steroid prized in bodybuilding for lean gains with fewer side effects; human trials exist only in anemia, cancer and rehabilitation.
lead: Methenolone (also metenolone; brand name Primobolan) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone, available as an oral acetate and an injectable enanthate ester. Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, describes it as a relatively mild androgen introduced medically in the early 1960s for anemias and wasting.
claims: Primobolan is a milder, safer steroid.
It builds lean muscle.
Primobolan is harsh on lipids.
